title: Introduce SSL compatibility shim to decouple runtime from system OpenSSL and orchestrate JWK rotation for signed tokens
creator: Aisha Gupta
description: Problem: Multiple services implicitly link against the host system libssl/libcrypto. This causes unpredictable behavior between cloud images, container base images, and on-prem bundles and blocks us from shipping a FIPS-compatible runtime. Additionally, our JWK rotation process for signing keys is manual and has led to two incidents where stale public keys caused auth failures for internal API consumers. Goal: 1) Add a lightweight SSL compatibility shim (runtime-level adapter) that allows the inference runtime to load a controlled crypto provider (bundled OpenSSL or BoringSSL build) at startup without relying on the system linker. 2) Implement an automated JWK rotation orchestration flow that pushes rotated keys to the trust stores used by the auth-service and runtime, with observability and rollback. This ticket covers design, implementation, tests, canary rollout, and documentation updates.
steps: Design compatibility shim: define adapter API, TLS stack abstraction surfaces, and supported provider contracts
Create a minimal loader that resolves symbols at runtime and falls back to a validated bundled OpenSSL/BoringSSL if system libssl is incompatible
Add build targets and packaging for a vetted OpenSSL build (static) and a BoringSSL variant for on-prem images
Refactor auth-service and runtime token verification path to use the shim API instead of direct OpenSSL calls
Implement JWK rotation orchestrator: operator service + idempotent publisher that updates runtime and auth-service caches
Add migration path: compatibility mode that keeps old verification enabled for 48h during rollout
Create integration tests: signed token acceptance tests against both system and bundled providers, plus negative tests for malformed keys
Performance benchmark: run token verification microbenchmarks and end-to-end latency tests before/after to ensure <5% regression
Security review and dependency SBOM update
Canary rollout: enable shim and orchestrator for 1% traffic, monitor auth errors and latency for 72 hours, then 10%/50%/100%
Update runbooks, Confluence design doc, and RFC for future FIPS build plans
acceptance_criteria: Runtime no longer fails to start when host libssl versions differ between build and deploy images (verified across three distro images)
Automated JWK rotation publishes new keys and all dependent services fetch and validate new keys without manual intervention
No more than 5% regression in median token verification latency in benchmarks
Security team sign-off on the shim implementation and the bundled provider builds
End-to-end resilience verified via canary rollout (no auth regressions, SLOs maintained)
All changes documented in the runtime security Confluence page and SBOM updated in the repo
notes: Trade-offs: introducing a shim increases maintenance surface but buys us deterministic crypto behavior across environments and enables FIPS bundling later.

We evaluated alternatives: (a) force standard base images (rejected due to enterprise on-prem constraints), (b) patch each downstream package to avoid direct OpenSSL calls (high churn), (c) shim approach (chosen).
Review feedback from infra team: ensure loader has strict symbol whitelist and fails closed if unexpected ABI is detected.
Edge-case: some transitive Python extensions load libssl via dlopen; plan includes a compatibility test matrix for Python 3.11/3.12 images.
Coordination: sync with release engineering to include the bundled provider in publish pipelines for dedicated and private deploys.
